exploration_data/reachable_mask.npz.note: Denominator 4,002,095 -> 3,757,990 (-244,105): the REAL-ARC ENVELOPE. Methods B/C bound a jump by a rectangle (rise 183 AND reach 480 at once); no arc does both. Re-derived from 228 measured engine arcs (exploration_data/jump_arcs.npz, tools/collect_jump_arcs.py) with a generous bound (arcs slide along walls, every arc launchable from every standable anchor). It accounts for 99.74% of the 3.16M px of real play on the 14.8M state; the 8,274 px it denies are kept as observed play (exploration_data/observed_reach.npz), so coverage is lossless. The 244,105 removed px are all classified CONNECTIVITY_GAP (model gap, never a glitch). Applied by tools/build_reachability.py --tighten; the previous rectangle-envelope mask is archived at exploration_data/archive_mask_v3_rectangle/reachable_mask.npz. PREVIOUS NOTE: Denominator 4,013,723 -> 4,002,095, from two independent corrections that nearly cancel. (1) BOTH OF MARIO'S FORMS: A/B/C and the noncoverage classifier ran on the small collider (30x40) only, while coverage records the real per-form collider; big Mario (40x80) reaches 40 px higher, so ordinary big-Mario play was classified ANOMALOUS - 25,356 px in one measured run, every one inside the big envelope. Method B 4,097,097 -> 4,252,679. (2) FLAG TRIGGER: checkpoint '11' is a 6x600 rect at x 8504 spanning the whole level height; past it Mario is under the scripted flag sequence, so only the grab band (to x 8564) and the recorded slide-and-walk corridor are reachable - removes 167,210 px. Acceptance: no coverage state lost a covered pixel, and the worst anomalous count across 9 states fell from 25,356 to 2. Superseded masks kept under exploration_data/archive_*. Fingerprint ded5cd19...
